beats.text: Get attacked in public, and nobody helps? Nope! That's a myth.
Researchers analyzed security camera footage of two hundred and nineteen real street fights, in three countries.
In nine out of ten, at least one stranger stepped in!
And here's the twist: the more people were around, the more likely someone helped!
So strangers do show up. Next time, be one of them!

sources: Philpot, Liebst, Levine, Bernasco & Lindegaard (2020). Would I be helped? Cross-national CCTV footage shows that intervention is the norm in public conflicts. American Psychologist 75(1). 219 conflicts in Amsterdam, Cape Town, Lancaster; at least one intervener in ~91%; ~3.76 interveners on average; more bystanders -> higher odds of help. Via PsyPost.
